output.summary: KEP-2485 introduces a ReadWriteOncePod PersistentVolume access mode that restricts a volume to a single pod on a single node, distinct from ReadWriteOnce which allows many pods on one node. The KEP is implemented and at stage stable.
output.rationale: Existing ReadWriteOnce allows simultaneous access from many pods on one node, so a single-pod guarantee was missing. The KEP adds the new access mode and CSI spec changes (SINGLE_NODE_SINGLE_WRITER) while keeping ReadWriteOnce working. Reviewers pushed for scheduler-time enforcement and version-skew analysis, and the scheduler enforcement was added during the alpha/beta work.

alternatives.option: Not introducing a SINGLE_NODE_MULTI_WRITER access mode in the CSI spec and keeping SINGLE_NODE_WRITER
alternatives.why_not: The readme says SINGLE_NODE_WRITER has conflicting definitions, and introducing SINGLE_NODE_SINGLE_WRITER was the chance to fix that confusion.

alternatives.option: Keep the feature in alpha for one more release, then target beta in 1.27
alternatives.why_not: Maintainer msau42 said tests had to be implemented and running before beta promotion, so beta was moved from 1.26 to 1.27 rather than skipped.

alternatives.option: Tracking a selected-pod annotation on PVCs to speed up PVC protection checks
alternatives.why_not: Chrishenzie said it was not GA-blocking for this feature and that the problem is not unique to this access mode, so it was decoupled.

evidence.quote: This KEP introduces a new ReadWriteOncePod access mode for PersistentVolumes that restricts access to a single pod on a single node.
This access mode differs from the existing ReadWriteOnce (RWO) access mode, which restricts access to a single node, but allows simultaneous access from many pods on that node.
Beta graduation will need to happen in 1.27, see here for more context: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3537#discussion_r978120310
it looks like we can consider this project independently of ReadWriteOncePod (we're not considering it GA-blocking for this feature).
Would it halt? I think from the comment above, it looks like scheduler will not enforce if the feature gate is disabled.
